section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 1. Does your program have a mission statement?
question_notes: Our mission statement at 18 Degrees provides the foundation for all the work we do, including mentoring. Our mission - "We champion access, opportunity, belonging, and well-being for all people on their journey, helping to build thriving communities" which was recently updated as part of our current strategic plan, speaks to inclusivity and building community. Our approach with our folks, including our mentees, is to start with questions about their goals – their dreams. Our work is to guide them to the resources, skills, and support that will help them reach their goals.  This is central to our mission to help those we serve see that new beginnings are possible.

section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 2. Does your program have a logic model that describes the key components, activities, and outcomes of the program in a graphic or illustration?
question_notes: Our current logic model needs to be updated to reflect our expanded mentoring program and the changes we are making to deepen our impact throughout the agency.

section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 3. Does your program have a Theory of Change (i.e., a comprehensive description/illustration that articulates how the young people being served reach their short- and long-term outcomes as a result of the program’s work)?
question_notes: Our current theory does a good job of explaining the mentoring program's rationale, activities, the results of these activities, and the intended changes/improvements we hope our youth gain from participating in the program.

section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 4. Does your program have a manual that documents your program’s written policies and procedures?
question_notes: We have a relatively comprehensive policies and procedures manual for 18 Degrees Mentoring. However, there are a couple of areas in particular with opportunities for improvement. Match support and supervision procedures should be further developed and more clearly defined, as well as our evaluation procedures.

section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 5. Does your program review your program policies and procedures on a set schedule, at least one time per year?
question_notes: With recent staffing changes to our mentoring program, I am unable to say definitively how often the policies and procedures were reviewed. I can say that going forward it will be reviewed a minimum of once per year.

section_title: A. Mentoring Program Design and Implementation
question_text: 6. Have your program’s policies and procedures been reviewed with respect to inclusiveness of potentially vulnerable populations, such as LGBTQ+ individuals, those with disabilities, youth and mentors of color, immigrants and refugees, and/or other often marginalized groups?
question_notes: Our policies and procedures, as well as our volunteer guidelines, were written with inclusivity in mind, however, there is always much room for improvement in this area. Specifically, in the areas of mentor recruitment.

question_text: 7. Does your program have a written mentee recruitment plan?
question_notes: We do not have a written mentee recruitment plan. Traditionally, recruitment has happened through referrals to the program from schools, word of mouth (self- referral), and outreach in the community by staff.

question_text: 8. Does your program provide prospective mentees (and their parents/guardians, when applicable) with the eligibility requirements for participation so that youth and their families can determine their fit for the program?
question_notes: Intake for the mentoring program begins with an explanation of the eligibility requirements from the Pittsfield Community Connection Services Coordinator who first speaks with the mentee's caregiver followed by a conversation with the mentee.  From there the mentor coordinator meets with the both the mentee and caregiver to ensure the youth and family still feel they are a fit. Finally, the mentee and caregiver are introduced the to the mentor where the mentor coordinator will again review requirements and check in to ensure everyone still feels they are ready, comfortable, and committed to begin meeting with their mentor.

question_text: 9. Does your program’s youth recruitment materials use inclusive and welcoming language for mentees that realistically portray the expectations and responsibilities of participating in the program?
question_notes: Our youth recruitment materials are distributed through the Pittsfield Community Connection program which includes mentoring as a service. Our materials are reviewed at several levels of management especially around inclusive language and diversity. We are currently in the process of expanding our mentoring program beyond PCC to include our Family Resource Center with a focus on deepening the impact and inclusiveness of the program.

question_text: 10. Does your program have a written mentor recruitment plan?
question_notes: I8 Degrees mentoring has a written recruitment plan which includes using several different types of promotional materials such as flyers, a newsletter, social media, and the 18 Degrees website. Recruitment efforts are made in the community by both the mentor coordinator and the director of volunteer services. The plan includes several activities such as attending community events, flyer distribution, and presenting to local businesses and community organizations. The rating of 3 indicates the need for our recruitment of a more diverse volunteer base.

question_text: 11. Does your program provide prospective mentors with a “job description” that explains the mentor’s role and eligibility criteria?
question_notes: We provide mentors with a job description during the interview process and again during the mentor training. The description covers the mentor's role, participation requirements, time commitment, benefits, and the application and screening process.

question_text: 12. Does your program’s mentor recruitment materials realistically portray the expectations and responsibilities of participating in the program?
question_notes: Our recruitment materials list the essential requirements for being a mentor - age, time commitment, and the need to be a consistent, positive role model the life of a youth.

question_text: 13. Has your program developed and/or implemented strategies for increasing the diversity of its mentors (e.g. race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, socio-economic, etc.)?
question_notes: Our mentor coordinator and director of volunteer services attend a variety of community events such as Pride, Westside Legends community day, and other various community events throughout the year. This is an area with big opportunities for growth.

question_text: 14. Does your program have established, written criteria for assessing the fit of mentees and families for the program?
question_notes: Our Pittsfield Community Connection services coordinator meets with and assesses the fit for participation in our PCC program which includes mentoring services (using written criteria). The services coordinator will then meet with the referral team (including an LICSW clinician) to determine the young person fit for the PCC program/mentoring.  If a participant does not meet the criteria for PCC, they may be referred to our Family Resource Center where the FRC manager will continue the assessment process to determine the best FRC group enrollment. All participants in the mentoring services must also be enrolled in a program at 18 Degrees -ensuring that the youth and their families have wrap around supports in place.

question_text: 15. Does your program offer an in-person or virtual orientation to prospective mentees (and parents/guardians, when relevant) in which they can learn details about the program to determine if they are a good fit for the experience?
question_notes: All youth being enrolled in Pittsfield Community Connection or Family Resource Center programs are given an in-person description of our mentoring services ideally by the mentor coordinator or by the intake staff member if the mentor coordinator is unavailable.

question_text: 16. Does your program require a written application that gathers information about the mentee and their hopes for the program experience?
question_notes: We gather written information from the mentee at intake and during the pre-match process on their goals and hopes for participation in the mentorship program.

question_text: 17. Does your program collect relevant demographic data about potential mentees (e.g., race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, disability, etc.)?
question_notes: Yes, we gather this information during the intake process (and is followed up with at the pre-match to ensure we have as much information as the youth and family are comfortable sharing), it is then entered and tracked in our database system called FAMCare.

question_text: 18. Does your program conduct an interview with youth (and parents/guardians, when relevant) to learn more about the youth’s needs and goals for the program experience?
question_notes: Yes, the mentor coordination completes an in-depth pre-match meeting with the youth and caregivers. The youth's outreach/case manager or other trusted adult within the program they are enrolled also offers to attend for addition support. These pre-match meetings are a time for the youth and family to gain a better understanding of the program and for staff to get to know the youth allowing the youth time to share their needs and goals (orally and written).

question_text: 19. Does your program require mentees (and parents/guardians, when relevant) to agree in writing to the expectations and responsibilities of participating in the program and working with their mentor(s)?
question_notes: Yes, during the match meeting a written agreement is signed by the mentee, caregiver and the mentor. Expectations, responsibilities, and goals are set at this time. A copy of this agreement is given to the mentee, mentor, and the youth's caregiver.

question_text: 20. Does your program have written, established criteria for assessing the fit of mentors with the program and for disqualifying potential mentors as needed?
question_notes: We have written criteria for our volunteer mentors. It is explained to all new potential mentors that the screening process (for them and for us) begins with the mentor interview and background check and continues through the training and matching process. It is explained that if 18 Degrees mentoring staff determines the volunteer is not a good fit they can be disqualified at any point. We encourage mentors to screen us for fit as well.

question_text: 21. Does your program offer an in-person or virtual orientation to prospective mentors in which they can learn details about the program and determine if they are a good fit for the experience?
question_notes: We have a virtual volunteer orientation for the 18 Degrees agency with a presentation offered by the mentor coordinator (highlighting the details about the mentoring program).

question_text: 22. Does your program require potential mentors to complete a written application that gathers information relevant to their ability to provide youth with a safe mentoring experience and their suitability for participating in the program?
question_notes: Yes, our online written volunteer application is extensive and requires three references.

question_text: 23. Does your program collect relevant demographic data about potential mentors (e.g., race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, disability, socioeconomic status, etc.)?
question_notes: Yes, this information is requested on the mentor application and is tracked in our volunteer database.

question_text: 24. Does your program conduct at least one face-to-face interview with potential mentors?
question_notes: The interview is conducted by the mentor coordinator and the director of volunteer services. All interviews require two interviewers be present. All interviews are conducted in person. We asked questions about the prospective mentor's growing up years and their familial and personal relationships. We always add the disclaimer that they are only being asked to share as much as they feel comfortable but the more we can learn, the better the match will be.

question_text: 25. Does your program conduct a comprehensive criminal history records check on potential mentors prior to acceptance in the mentoring program, at a minimum searching a state criminal records database, along with sex offender and child abuse registries?
question_notes: Yes, all mentors are required to complete a national background check through the Datafacts system, a CORI, a SORI, and a driver's record check - including insurance.

question_text: 26. Does your program conduct at least two reference checks (personal and/or professional) on potential mentors?
question_notes: We request three references from all volunteer mentors - we require a minimum of two be completed and reviewed before matching.

question_text: 27. Does your program utilize any other screening checks or procedures relevant to your program model?
28. Does your program require mentors to agree in writing to the expectations and responsibilities of participating in the program and working with their mentee(s)?
question_notes: Yes, Mentors sign an agreement along with their mentees and caregivers agreeing to the expectations and responsibilities of the program.

question_text: 29. Does your program ensure that screening processes for mentors follow ethical, professional, and legal standards regarding information sharing and confidentiality?
question_notes: Yes, all volunteer records kept by the mentor coordinator are locked and confidential. Background information is not kept in the mentor's file but is housed in our HR department with employee records. The same protocols are followed for volunteers as for staff.

question_text: 30. Does your program require training for mentees that prepares them to be successful in their role as a mentee in the program?
question_notes: We cover all of the above during the pre-match meeting. This is not a separate training, but it might be helpful if we held it as such.

question_text: 31. Does your mentee training review program rules and risk management policies?
question_notes: We cover the above topics with the mentee and their caregiver during the pre-match meeting. Some of the details are also covered again during the match meeting and discussed with the mentee, caregiver, and mentor in the same room. We do this before they all sign the final mentoring agreement.

question_text: 32. Does your program provide ongoing training or learning opportunities for mentees throughout their participation in the program?
question_notes: Mentees are offered an array of opportunities for training and learning through our youth development programs. These are programs the youth are enrolled in coordination with mentoring and are a part of the wrap around service offered to the youth and families.

question_text: 33. Does your program require at least two hours of pre-mentoring relationship training that prepares mentors to be successful in their role?
question_notes: We hold a 3+ hour training session that all mentors must complete prior to being matched with a mentee.

question_text: 34. Does your program training inform mentors about program rules and risk management policies?
question_notes: These topics are all covered in the training and talked about again during the match meeting ensuring everyone is understanding of the expectations prior to signing the mentoring agreement.

question_text: 35. Does your program provide ongoing training opportunities to mentors throughout their participation in the program?
question_notes: We offer a minimum of two trainings per year on the above-mentioned topics. We've had trainings hosted through 18 Degrees as well as the Institute for Health and Recovery, Mass Mentoring Partnership and other community organizations. We continue to struggle with what to host virtually and what to hold in person in order to gain the best participation. We currently do a mix of both.

question_text: 36. Does your program have established, documented criteria for forming mentoring relationships between mentors with mentees, either in pairs or groups?
question_notes: The 18 Degrees Mentoring program has established, documented criteria for forming mentoring relationships as outlined in the policies and procedures manual beginning on page 40. The mentor coordinator provides an additional layer of safety in mentoring matches through consideration of gender (we do not make female mentee/male mentee matches and extra assessment of safety for LGBTQ+ matches (with advisement from our clinician and/or LGBTQ coordinator).

question_text: 37. Does your program share information about the proposed mentoring relationship(s) with mentors, mentees, and (when appropriate) parent(s)/guardians to prepare participants for their initial meeting?
question_notes: Yes, initial information about relationships is shared with the mentors, mentees and parent/guardians prior to their initial meeting. Our goal is to ensure there are no surprises that might potentially derail a match at the match meeting. By sharing this initial information, we hope to determine if any barriers to successful match exist prior to the match meeting.

question_text: 38. Does your program arrange and document an initial meeting, facilitated by program staff that includes the mentor(s) and mentee(s), as well as parent(s)/guardian(s) (when appropriate)?
question_notes: Yes, our match meetings are arranged by the mentor coordinator and include the mentee, caregiver, and mentor. The mentoring Agreement is completed by the mentor and mentee during the match meeting and is signed by all parties. A copy is given to the mentee, caregiver and the mentor.

question_text: 39. Does your program have the mentor(s) and mentee(s), as well as parents/guardians when appropriate, sign a relationship commitment agreement at the initial meeting?
question_notes: Yes, as stated above all parties complete the agreement which includes the mentor/mentee's first activity and time/date they will meet. Contact information and preferred method of contact is also provided for all parties.

question_text: 40. Does your program provide information to parents/guardians about program rules, risk management policies, and their responsibilities in supporting the mentoring relationship?
question_notes: Parents/guardians are given both written and verbal explanations of the program rules and risk management policies as well as signing appropriate release forms.

question_text: 41. Does your program regularly engage parents/guardians in the program through information sharing, invitations to special events, sharing progress about their child, or other engagement opportunities?
question_notes: Our mentor coordinator strives to stay in touch with parents and guardians in order to provide support in the mentoring relationship. Contact is generally made through phone calls and texts. We could certainly do more to engage families - some of the suggestions above seem like great ideas.

question_text: 42. Does your program check in separately with mentors twice a month for the first month of the mentoring relationship and monthly thereafter (or at a consistent interval appropriate to the nature of the program and the safety needs and risk level of participants)?
question_notes: Yes, the mentor coordinator checks in with new mentors at a minimum of 2 times per month (but often it is more) to ensure that folks are meeting, to address any concerns, and to support the mentor. After the first few months, the mentor coordinator will check in a minimum of once a month. We also require mentors to report their hours, activities and a summary of their meetings to the mentor coordinator following each outing.

question_text: 43. Does your program check in separately, and in developmentally appropriate ways, with mentees twice a month for the first month of the mentoring relationship and monthly thereafter (or at a consistent interval appropriate to the nature of the program and the safety needs and risk level of participants)?
question_notes: Yes, our program staff - mentor coordinator and case managers - will check in with mentees regularly (minimum of 2 times a month in the beginning) to assure the match is going well and to assess safety needs of the participants. As matches continue program staff will check in monthly.

question_text: 44. Does your program check in with another responsible adult in the mentee’s life (e.g., parent, guardian, teacher, counselor, etc.) at a minimum of twice a month in the first month of the mentoring relationship and at least quarterly thereafter (or at a consistent interval appropriate to the nature of the program and the safety needs and risk level of participants)?
question_notes: The mentor coordinator makes every effort to check in with the mentee's caregiver twice a month in the beginning of the match, however, it can sometimes be difficult to get responses. The program staff makes every effort to check in a minimum of once a month for new matches.

question_text: 45. Does your program use a standardized protocol at each contact (with mentors, mentees, and responsible adults) that collects information and elicits conversation about mentor and mentee activities, safety concerns, and relationship progress?
question_notes: We complete the check ins however we do not have a standardized form for each contact. This is something that we should be develop.

question_text: 46. At each contact (with mentors and mentees) does your program provide access to relevant resources (i.e. expert advice from program staff or others, publications, web-based resources, experienced mentors) to support the participant and the mentoring relationship and/or help address needs and challenges as they arise?
question_notes: Yes, our mentor coordinator provides access to resources and will elicit help from other program staff and community partners as needed.

question_text: 47. Does your program document all contacts with participants by gathering relevant information (e.g., meeting dates and activities, challenges and support provided, goals achieved, etc.) in an appropriate format accessible by relevant staff?
question_notes: All contacts with participants are entered as case notes (including meeting dates and activities) and documented in our FAMCare database which all relevant staff can access.

question_text: 48. Does your program have a process for ensuring that mentoring relationship support procedures are adhered to, and that program staff contact participants as required?
question_notes: The mentor coordinator receives weekly supervision from the director of volunteer services who reviews each match and ensures contacts are being made. The director will also assist the mentor coordinator in making contacts as needed and address concerns as they arise.

question_text: 49. Does your program conduct additional activities to support mentors or mentoring relationships throughout the year?
question_notes: Our program attempts to provide 2-3 mentor/mentee group activities per year. We offer monthly mentor meetings for peer support and guidance from staff. The PCC program also provides drop-in hours to all participants and often mentees attend and get to know each other outside of the program. We also have mentor/mentees that meet as pair groups to attend community events or other activities. These pair outings help to build relationships for both mentors and mentees outside of just their match.

question_text: 50. Does your program regularly recognize and thank program participants for their contributions, such as with occasional thank-you cards, other gifts or tokens of recognition, or end-of-year celebration events?
question_notes: We host a yearly mentor/mentee dinner during National Mentoring Month in January hand out gift cards for an activity (such as movie passes or a dining GC). We also hold a Volunteer Appreciation event in April (food is served, we have a Thank You speech from our board chair and our CEO) during national volunteer week. We send birthday cards to all mentors. GCs are also distributed to participants throughout the year.

question_text: 51. Does your program evaluate whether mentoring relationships should be “renewed” or formally closed, emphasizing participant desires, at the end of each typical cycle?
question_notes: Yes, at the end of one-year (and each subsequent year) participants are evaluated to determine whether or not they would like to continue the mentoring relationship. If it is determined that the relationship will close - participants are brought back together for a formal closure meeting.

question_text: 52. Does your program have written protocols for handling a variety of closure circumstances, including anticipated and/or unanticipated closures, scenarios in which participants are willing/unwilling, or able/unable to engage in a closure process and goodbye meeting?
question_notes: Yes, we have written protocols for a variety of closure circumstances.

question_text: 53. Does your program prepare and/or coach mentors, mentees, and parents/guardians (when relevant) for a final goodbye meeting or other closure activities?
question_notes: We try to hold a "healthy closure" meeting whenever possible. This meeting is facilitated by the mentor coordinator and provides the opportunity for everyone to come back together and reflect on their experience and process feelings. We understand that it is a crucial aspect of the mentoring relationship.

question_text: 54. Does your program have established criteria for whether and how participants should be re-matched and procedures for how re-matching is done?
question_notes: Participants can be re-matched, after an evaluation by the mentor coordinator. Things such as past engagement are mentee needs evaluated.

question_text: 55. Does your program conduct exit interviews with mentors, mentees, and parents/guardians once the programmatic timeline ends?
question_notes: Due to a change in staffing for the mentor coordinator position, I am not sure exactly what was covered during exit interviews - I don't believe they were necessarily held "formally" or included outcome assessments. This is an area for growth for our program.

question_text: 56. Does your program document all relationship closures and exits from the program in the program’s information management system, including the date of exit and if relationships are no longer reported as active in reporting and evaluation?
question_notes: All program closures are documented in our database system and after closure are made inactive.

question_text: 57. Does your program have a board of directors or advisory committee that operates with clear roles and responsibilities and meets on a regularly scheduled basis?
question_notes: Yes, 18 Degrees has a 18-member board of directors with clear roles and responsibilities who meet quarterly. Further information on board roles and demographics can be provided upon request.

question_text: 58. Does your program’s board of directors provide adequate resources and governance to support the program?
question_notes: Yes, our board provides a wide range of resources and provides governance to support the agency which in turn supports the mentoring program.

question_text: 59. Do the members of your program’s board of directors or advisory committee reflect the diversity of the community being served and the mentors and mentees participating in the program?
question_notes: It is the goal of 18 Degrees to champion inclusion, diversity, equity, and access in all areas of the agency including our board of directors. 18 Degrees supports a culture of Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA) for our board, staff and our participants.

question_text: 60. Does your program’s board of directors or advisory committee regularly assess and balance its composition by race/ethnicity, gender, sexuality, ability, etc.?
question_notes: Discussion of balancing the board's composition while supporting diversity is an ongoing conversation.

question_text: 61. Are youth represented on your board of directors or advisory committee or offered other meaningful opportunities to provide input into program leadership and/or decisions?
question_notes: We do not have youth members on our board of directors, however our youth development program has a youth leadership council that meet regularly to provide feedback and guidance to our senior team and board members.

question_text: 62. Does the staff of your program reflect the diversity of the community being served and the mentors and mentees participating in the program?
question_notes: 18 Degrees supports a culture of Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, and Access (IDEA) for both our staff and our participants. 18 Degrees hires staff from the communities where we work, valuing lived experience and community knowledge in our selection process. Working with our staff who have lived experience allows participants to feel they matter, and provides them with a model of life success, giving them hope and fostering empowerment.  We coach participants to develop skills needed to be good advocates for their families, and to bring their voice to the table. Hiring staff with lived experience helps to build trusting relationships with participants who reflect similar backgrounds and shared experiences, including a cultural standpoint and shared language. We actively recruit employees who speak languages in addition to English, with Spanish being the most common.  We pay a language differential to employees who speak languages in addition to English

question_text: 63. Does program leadership (or the board of directors) regularly assess its organization and leadership composition by race/ethnicity, gender, sexuality, ability, etc.?
question_notes: Yes, program leadership is regularly assessing its composition for diversity, Equity and inclusion.

question_text: 64. Does your organization have strategies and policies in place to recruit and retain staff of color, including leadership?
question_notes: Having a representative board and workforce strengthens our commitment and our capacity to support our community. Within our agency, 33% of our 156 employees identify as BIPOC. On our eight-person senior leadership team, 38% identify as BIPOC and 63% are women. On our seventeen-person board of directors, 65% of members are women, and 24% identify as BIPOC.

question_text: 65. Does your program have a history of retaining staff members over time?
question_notes: Yes, in our youth development program, which includes mentoring, many of our staff have been with 18 Degrees five years or longer. A few have exceeded the ten-year mark. Our staff's growth is supported through the formation of a Leadership Cohort which is now in its third year. Staff completing the cohort training have gone to expanded positions within the agency and some have found growth in the community. It is the goal of 18 Degrees to support staff on their professional journey.

question_text: 66. Does your program have adequate staffing for the number of mentoring relationships being served currently, allowing the program to implement services with fidelity and consistency?
question_notes: Yes, our mentoring program recently expanded to include a director-level position to provide assistance, support, and oversight for the mentor coordinator. The director of volunteer services has the responsibility for reporting, assisting with grant writing, budgeting, and more allowing the mentor coordinator to focus efforts on supporting and growing the program's mentoring relationships.

question_text: 67. Do all staff members have relevant backgrounds and education for the roles they are filling?
question_notes: The director of volunteer services has a bachelor's degree in criminal justice and human services, has worked in volunteer management for over eight years, and has been a mentor in the program for almost five years. The mentor coordinator has is currently working on her bachelor's in social work and was previously employed as a community health worker and community resource provider for the city of Pittsfield.

question_text: 68. Does your program offer onboarding training for all staff members, as well as ongoing training and professional development opportunities?
question_notes: Yes, our staff members are provided with onboarding training at the program level (90 day) and at the agency level (half-day training). Our agency's current leadership cohort recently developed a new onboarding template to ensure that all staff members receive inclusive training. We also hold an annual staff development day; every program has a budget for staff development; we use the Relias training system .

question_text: 69. Does your program provide program leadership and staff with training on issues of diversity, equity, inclusion, and cultural responsiveness?
question_notes: Yes, as mentioned above, our agency values our IDEA (Inclusion, Diversity, Equity and Access) work. In an effort to support this 18 Degrees has begun affinity groups including the IDEA task force, Lived Experience, Supervision and Leadership, and Motivational Interviewing. Each group attends regular meetings to take a deeper dive into issues and concerns related to their group. Groups also attend trainings on their specific topic then share the knowledge they gained with the larger group. Affinity groups are peer led and supported and guided by our VP of programs.

question_text: 70. Does your program have policies and/or procedures in place for addressing discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender identity/sexuality, national origin, disability, and/or age (e.g., workplace hostility, advancement, whistle-blower policy, communications, etc.)?
question_notes: Yes, our Human Resources department recently updated our employee handbook to include all of the above (available upon request). This is reviewed with new employees during the hiring process and during the agency orientation training. A digital copy is also available to employees through a shared Teams folder. Every employee is also required to complete workplace harassment training, whistle-blower policy, and effective communication through our Relias training system.

question_text: 71. Does your program implement appropriate community engagement strategies to ensure that it is part of the larger youth support ecosystem in your community?
question_notes: The 18 Degrees mentoring program is supported by our youth development team and all team members do outreach of some type in the community. This includes working and partnering with the local schools, the DA's office, the YMCA, the juvenile court, and other community stakeholders. Members of the youth development team are on the board of directors for other youth serving organizations. The team regularly hosts and attends community events. We also have a Pittsfield Community Connection Steering Committee run by the VP of Youth Development which consists of staff and community stakeholders who meet quarterly to provide guidance, networking, and oversight.

question_text: 72. Does your program seek input from marginalized communities in programming development (i.e., interpretation of outcomes, communication materials, recruitment planning, training for participants)?
question_notes:
Yes, through conversations with our participant families, we learn about the changing needs of our growing populations & identify new ways to support them.  We serve families from a variety of cultural & linguistic backgrounds, working to understand their needs & to help them feel welcome. For example, because the Latino/a/x community was identified as an underserved & growing population in western Mass., our programs employ bi-lingual, Spanish-speaking staff to deliver the program in our families’ primary language whenever possible. We also use interpretive services to ensure families can access information, attend programming, & maintain communication in their preferred language whenever we do not have an in-house staff member to meet those needs.  
 
18 Degrees values and encourages our participants’ voices in our planning & decision-making. Families are experts in their own lives, & we consider staff to be guides to help them discover their skills & strengths.  Our relationships with families are based on partnership & collaboration & we remind them of the voluntary nature of our services.  We set clear expectations together to define our role & the responsibilities of the family.  We provide consistent information & are accessible to families in many ways – phone, text, emails, & in–person or virtual visits.  Our staff stays flexible to meet their needs yet provides the structure to contradict the chaos that is often part of their lives.  Through this groundwork, we earn trust, so that when we ask for feedback, they can provide this honestly & openly.   
 
In addition to the various advisory groups described above, we receive more formal feedback from individual participants through annual satisfaction surveys. We target questions to seek information on service quality & culturally & linguistically appropriate service delivery. We ask if home visitors are respectful & sensitive when in their homes & amidst their culture. We follow up on their feedback to demonstrate the importance of their opinion & experience.

question_text: 73. Are program staff knowledgeable about historical and current traumas and injustices related to race, ethnicity, religion, gender identity/sexuality, national origin, disability, and/or age that may be experienced by mentees (& their families) within the areas they live (e.g. access or lack of access to resources for safe housing, advanced education, economic opportunities, transportation, health, public safety, food, etc.)?
question_notes: At 18 Degrees Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (EIB) is part of our agency-wide Inclusion, Diversity, Equity, & Access (IDEA) efforts & task force.  We understand that systemic oppression, redlining & other societal factors have led to a lack of generational wealth & perpetuated poverty among specific local populations. Our commitment to DEIB goes hand in hand with Trauma-Informed Care, integrating moving forward one step at a time with understanding the factors that contributed to an individual's situation, including struggles as well as strengths. Our goals include items that are part of our common practices & ensure we keep DEIB present in our workforce & the services we provide. Our agency shares this with staff through trainings that address root causes and use evidence-based practices throughout our work.

question_text: 74. Does your program have dedicated resources available to provide accommodations to increase accessibility for program participants as needed?
question_notes: Yes, the 18 Degrees mentoring program has access to many dedicated resources through our Pittsfield Community Connection program and our Family Resource Center. PCC provides transportation for youth to attend groups and drop-in hours; the program also has a washer and dryer available for participants use, provides gift cards to reinforce positive development, and meet youth where they by offering community outreach and non-traditional business hours. Similarly, our Family Resource Center works alongside parents, children, teens, caregivers and all individuals to access services within our agency or to other community services if needed.

question_text: 75. Does your program have a written communications and marketing plan?
question_notes: We do not have a written communications and marketing plan specifically for mentoring; however, the director of volunteer services role is supervised by the VP of Advancement and is a member of the advancement team. We meet regularly to discuss marketing and communication strategies.

question_text: 76. Do your program’s communication materials accurately portray the population of youth served and surrounding communities in varied media (website, social media, recruitment materials, staff communication) using asset-based language?
question_notes: It is the goal of 18 Degrees to always use asset-based language in all materials.  All forms of communication need to be approved by the VP of Advancement before being distributed.

section_title: O. Financial Management and Resource Development
question_text: 77. Does your program have a detailed annual program budget and formal accounting system?
question_notes: Mentoring services fall under the budgets of several programs - but is formally accounted for by each program director and overseen by the VP of Finance.

section_title: O. Financial Management and Resource Development
question_text: 78. Does your program have a formal resource development plan that details how the program will ensure it maintains its operating funds over time?
question_notes: 18 Degrees operates under a board approved budget for each fiscal year. Within the budget each program is funded individually through a variety of sources including grants, state funding, and donor contributions. Diversified funding produces stability. In the event of a short fall for any particular program 18 Degrees is committed to ensuring continuation of services through the efforts of our Grants and Outcome director and Advancement team who continually meet and work with individual programs to ensure successful funding. 18 Degrees also receives unrestricted funds that can help a program as needed.

section_title: O. Financial Management and Resource Development
question_text: 79. Does your program have a code of ethics or decision-making guidelines that govern your fundraising efforts (i.e., detailing what kinds of organizations you would not accept funding from)?
question_notes: Yes, we have a gift acceptance policy available for review if needed.

question_text: 80. Does your program have written policies and procedures for managing participant information and other records that reflect safety and confidentiality concerns?
question_notes: Confidentiality is of the highest concern to 18 Degrees. Our mentoring policies and procedures manual describes how we manage participant information and records. All participants files are locked and information such as case notes are maintained in a secure database called FAMCare.

question_text: 81. Does your program have a system, such as a database, for collecting and managing information about program participants, their relationships, and their program experience?
question_notes: Previously we have maintained participants information in the Optima database system - we have recently transitioned to using the FAMCare database.

question_text: 82. Does your program have a written evaluation and/or data collection plan?
question_notes: This is an area where our program would like to focus efforts for improvement. We need to develop better surveys and methods for measuring mentee and mentor outcomes. We currently have detailed information about relationship activities and regularly receive participant feedback, but the other areas offer a great opportunity for growth.
question_goal_name: Evaluation and Data Collection Plan Documentation

question_text: 83. Does your program use a mentoring relationship quality survey or questionnaire to assess the quality of the relationship at least once during each program year?
question_notes: We send out mentoring relationship quality surveys to mentors 2 times per year and to our mentees 1 time per year.

question_text: 84. Does your program use professionally developed data collection tools (i.e., validated surveys or “scales”) to measure participant outcomes?
question_notes: The surveys we have been using in our program were developed by our former mentor coordinator and were based on validated surveys. We have had support from Mass Mentoring for several years and I believe the MC worked with MMP to develop our surveys. However, I cannot confirm what surveys or scales they originated from.

question_text: 85. Does your program analyze program implementation data on a set schedule to refine program practices and troubleshoot problems?
question_notes: We analyze our data regularly for reporting purposes. However, refining program practices and troubleshooting was not always done on a regular schedule. We have made changes to the program that will help us address this, but there is an area where we would appreciate MMP's guidance and suggestions.

question_text: 86. Does your program examine youth outcomes through the lens of race/ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, disability, etc. to see how different groups of youth are experiencing the program?
question_notes: We approach our work with an equity lens, but this is an area where improved surveys could help us to better examine outcomes and evaluate how different youth are experiencing the program.

question_text: 87. Does your program share your evaluation findings with program stakeholders including participants, staff, board members, funders, etc.?
question_notes: Yes, we share our outcomes through our annual report, at community events, with our board at meetings, and with our funders through our reporting.
